text:
sania: quick idea 1: lightweight ingest-patch proxy. emit tiny patches (token remap + header) and lazily materialize normalized binaries only on demand. saves storage and keeps ingest fast. tradeoffs?

liam: sounds neat. runtime might need rehydrate-on-load. how do we avoid tail latency if many rehydrates happen?

zara: LRU cache on serving nodes + pre-warm during promotion. enterprise flag to always materialize on ingest.

adele: still need semantic checks. propose two-tier probes: cheap CPU smoke for everyone, short GPU micro-run if CPU flags or model > threshold.

mike: agree. also keep a tiny quantized CPU runtime for quick top-k overlap checks to avoid spinning GPUs unnecessarily.

ops-bot: note: ingest concurrency currently 12. mass rehydrates could spike queues. recommend burst queue + backoff + prioritized orgs.

liam: tokenizer handling: generate deterministic tokenizer signature (vocab+specials), emit inline remap patch + reversible map for replay. mark as semantic-risk if mapping changes generation order beyond epsilon.

sania: manifest will include checksums, token_sig, patch refs, and probe summary. runtime reads header-first to route (reject, patch-on-load, fallback).

zara: minimal gating metrics: top1/top5 overlap, logprob-delta on gold tokens, p50/p95 latency delta. thresholds per org.

adele: rule engine for decisions: YAML ordered predicates -> action (FAIL/WARN/AUTO-FIX). env- and org-scoped.

registry-bot: indexing note: adding "patches" field requires registry schema migration. use write-new, read-old+new pattern.

mike: canary plan: internal orgs first, shadow-run patched vs raw runtime 24-72h, compare overlap + errors, auto-rollback on drift.

sania: next steps: adele prototype remapper + reversible map; liam draft rule-yaml; zara write canary runbook; sania API sketch for ingest-patch-proxy. reconvene in 48h. :rocket:
